note: B1's acceptance bar: neighbor-search results (the set of (site, image, distance) tuples within a cutoff) must be bit-for-bit identical between the current O(n^2) exact search and any future cell-list implementation, on this exact triclinic case that chematic-crystal's own test suite already uses. Do not invent a new triclinic angle set -- reuse this one so the acceptance test can be a direct before/after diff against the existing test's own expected values, not a fresh derivation.

structure: NaCl rock salt, space group Fm-3m (No. 225)
note: Standard textbook NaCl lattice parameter (a=5.6402 Angstrom, room temperature). Two-atom primitive-like representation (conventional cubic cell requires the full 4+4 FCC basis; this row deliberately uses the minimal 2-site cell as the simplest possible non-trivial case). Acceptance test: an arbitrary 3x3 integer supercell transform (e.g. [[1,1,0],[1,-1,0],[0,0,2]], a non-diagonal matrix) applied to this structure must produce a structure whose minimum-image neighbor distances (Na-Cl nearest distance = a/2 = 2.8201 Angstrom) are unchanged from the un-transformed cell -- the single cleanest possible correctness check for B1's arbitrary-supercell feature, since NaCl's nearest-neighbor distance is a widely-published, unambiguous reference value.

structure: diamond cubic carbon, space group Fd-3m (No. 227)
note: Standard diamond lattice parameter (a=3.567 Angstrom). Acceptance test: feeding the two sites in reversed order ([0.25,0.25,0.25] first, [0.0,0.0,0.0] second) must produce the identical neighbor-search result set (same nearest-neighbor distance = a*sqrt(3)/4 = 1.5445 Angstrom, same total neighbor count within any given cutoff) regardless of input site order -- the periodic-structure analog of this project's existing atom-permutation-invariance discipline for molecules.

structure: hypothetical Fe/Ni disordered alloy site, BCC-like
note: Uses chematic-crystal's already-implemented Occupancy/SiteSpecies disorder model (site.rs, Occupancy::SUM_TOLERANCE = 1e-6 validation already enforced) -- this fixture does not require new occupancy machinery, only confirms that any future B1/B2 work (neighbor-search rewrite, structure matching) must preserve disorder-aware site status rather than silently collapsing a partial-occupancy site to a single species. Lattice parameter is a representative BCC iron-class value (a=2.87 Angstrom), not a claim about a specific published Fe-Ni alloy phase.

note: Standard FCC copper lattice parameter (a=3.6149 Angstrom), full 4-atom conventional cell. B2's eventual acceptance bar: a primitive-cell-finding function applied to this conventional cell must produce a rhombohedral primitive cell with exactly 1 atom and 1/4 the volume, and re-expanding that primitive cell back to the conventional setting must reproduce this exact 4-site structure (a round-trip identity check) -- this is the acceptance criterion this RFC's section 5 calls 'primitive/supercell identity,' pinned here with a structure simple enough to verify by hand if needed.

Deliberately near-degenerate rhombohedral cell (alpha differs from beta/gamma by only 0.0001 degree) -- a tolerance-boundary stress case for any future cell-reduction (B2, Niggli) or symmetry-detection (B3) work, chosen because near-degenerate cells are exactly where naive floating-point tolerance choices produce different answers on different machines/compilers. Not implementable against today's code (no reduction/symmetry-determination exists) -- pinned now so a future B2/B3 round has a concrete stress case from round zero, rather than discovering the need for one after an initial implementation already made an undocumented tolerance choice.
